messages:
devon: Heads-up — customer hit an odd double-charge pattern when a streaming response triggered a toolcall and then we retried after a KV eviction. billing dashboard shows tokens for both the partial stream and the retried toolcall. anyone seen this?
sasha: yep, saw a similar report from beta org yesterday. short version: router fell back to a cheaper encoding, stream truncated, client retried the toolcall, and ledger ended up with two charge entries.
kevin: do we have a reliable repro? need to know if it's a router ordering problem or our provisional crediting logic.
devon: repro attached by support (paraphrased): client opens stream -> server streams prefix A -> KV eviction drops cached prefix -> router falls back mid-stream to compat-model -> partial toolcall event emitted with provisional charge -> client retries toolcall once stream closed -> final toolcall charged too.
maria: can you paste the relevant logs? even a tiny snippet helps. :eyes:
devon: sure — here's the core trace we saw:
```
INFO  [router] session=ses_0xabc step=stream offset=406 fallback_model=redwood-compat-v2
DEBUG [billing] provisional_charge id=pc_134 toolcall=tc_987 tokens=132 status=partial
WARN  [kv] eviction key=ctx:ses_0xabc reason=memory_pressure
INFO  [router] retried_toolcall id=tc_987 retry_of=tc_987 attempt=2 tokens=125 final=yes
```
sasha: that matches my gut — provisional_charge created when part of stream emitted, but we never tied the provisional to a stable session ownership id that survives a fallback. when retry happens we create a final charge with same toolcall id but different ownership context so dedupe misses it.
kevin: telemetry currently emits these fields: session_id, toolcall_id, token_count, provisional_flag, model. missing: prefix_owner_id and stream_offset_snapshot. without those the ledger can't stitch partial->final.
maria: short-term mitigation: mark provisional charges in UI and exclude them from immediate invoice totals until reconciliation completes. ops-bot, can we add an alert when provisional-to-final ratio > 1.2 for a customer?
ops-bot: auto-alert rule proposal: if provisional_charges_count(customer, 1h) / final_charges_count(customer, 1h) > 1.15 then page #eng-platform on slack. created ticket #PLAT-4113 if accepted.
kevin: long-term fix idea: router should emit an ownership_prefix token that survives KV eviction/fallbacks. ledger dedupe key = (customer, ownership_prefix, toolcall_id, stream_offset_window). keep TTL ~30s.
sasha: agree. also make toolcall finalization idempotent server-side: finalization should be noop if a final charge with same dedupe key already exists. simpler than trying to change client retry behavior.
devon: UX ask for console folks: expose a "provisional credits" column in the per-route billing view and link to raw telemetry rows with ownership_prefix so SREs can debug. Right now the path from console -> raw logs is too manual.
maria: can we instead auto-resolve provisional credits when the ledger sees a matching final charge? then the console would just show reconciled totals. need to ensure we don't prematurely resolve in ambiguous cases.
kevin: plan proposal: (1) emit ownership_prefix + stream_offset_snapshot from router (2) ledger dedupe on (customer, prefix, toolcall_id, offset-window) (3) add provisional->final reconciliation job for TTL=60s that resolves credits and emits reconciliation events for audit (4) console: add provisional column + link to reconciliation events.
sasha: implementation notes: router change is ~3d, ledger change ~2d, reconciliation job ~1d, console front-end ~2d. prioritize router + ledger first.
devon: agree. can we also add a debug flag to the router so support can enable full ownership debug for a session (emit extra traces)? would speed repro.
maria: supportable. ops-bot, add toggle flag request flow in the internal runbook?
ops-bot: done — runbook updated: /runbooks/billing-debug -> added "router ownership debug" toggle steps. ticket updated PLAT-4113.
kevin: one more thought — what about streaming truncation where the client sends a truncated tool payload and we still count tokens for the truncated prefix? that can also cause overcharge. need unit tests for prefix-truncation billing.
sasha: yup, add unit tests + an integration test that simulates KV eviction mid-stream and ensures dedupe key prevents double charge.
devon: ok I'll spin up a short PR for the router emitter + an integration test and ping y'all. thanks. :thumbsup:
maria: thx. let's target a canary next week and surface metrics: provisional_rate, reconciliation_latency, double_charge_incidents.
